name: Cholas Unite the Kaveri Delta and defeat Pallava king
description: Aditya Chola unite small warlords through incentives (shared loot from raids), killing the Pallava king, and claiming Sangam-era Chola lineage

name: Cholas Defeat Pandyas
description: United Kaveri Delta cartel defeats exhausted Pandyas; Parantaka even tries to raid Sri Lanka

name: Rashtrakuta Invasion of Tamil Nadu
description: Rashtrakutas decimate Chola army, kill crown prince Rajaditya, drive Parantaka from Thanjavur, reach Rameswaram; leave inscription; keep Tondai Nadu as buffer zone

name: Fall of the Rashtrakutas
description: Warlord Taila II from northern frontier defeats Rashtrakuta king Krishna III, ransacks capital and initiates the rise of the Kalachuri dynasty; creates power vacuum south of Vindhyas; Cholas had nothing to do with it but benefited

name: Chola Peak: Plunder in All Directions
place: Gangavadi, Bengal coast, Sri Lanka, Chera territory, Indonesia, Malaysia
description: Without Rashtrakutas to stop them, Cholas plunder north (Rashtrakuta territory), northeast (Bengal coast), south (Pandya + Sri Lanka), west (Chera territory + Arabian Sea), and overseas (Indonesia/Malaysia on merchant ships). Under rulers Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, this became the golden age of Chola expansion.

name: Chola Revenue System Overhaul
place: Kaveri Delta, Tondai Nadu, Nadu Nadu
description: Cholas dismantle centuries-old Nadu institutions and local warlord loyalties; establish centralized revenue secretariat cutting out middlemen; the Variyappad system replaces local control; farmer's 20 sacks now go directly to Chola coffers instead of split with local warlord and Nadu assembly

name: Chola Overseas Raid (Indonesia/Malaysia)
description: Chola army carried on merchant ships raids Southeast Asia; merchants of the 500 guild (a major trading collective) then harvest camphor and dominate sea routes to China, expanding merchant activity across the Indian Ocean; only known Indian dynasty to conduct trans-oceanic military raids

name: Construction of Thanjavur Periya Kovil
description: Rajaraja builds massive temple standing 65 meters tall with a gilded cupola; Meikirti inscriptions on walls serve as power projection to distant villages

name: Chola Fall and Later Pandya Revival
description: After period of Chola dominance, Pandyas return to power in Madurai; "Later Pandya" period begins, marking the end of Chola hegemony and the rise of regional powers; last Chola King reportedly disappeared into the forest (basis for Aayirathil Oruvan movie)

name: Pandyas fall to Sultanates. Madurai Sultanate Established
description: Delhi Sultanate forces sent south;  defeat Pandyas; governor declares independence; priests wall up real Siva Lingam in Meenakshi Temple and install duplicate; raiders desecrate fake (still visible as exhibit)

name: Vijayanagara Drives Out Madurai Sultanate
description: Vijayanagara army drives out Sultanate and restores the Pandyas as vassal states for the next century, establishing political order in the region and consolidating Vijayanagara's southern dominance

name: Dutch Occupy Pondicherry (and mint coins)
description: Dutch held Puducherry for 6 years and issued coins with "Pudu" in Tamil on reverse and Dutch Kali iconography on obverse

name: Vijayanagara Pagoda System Adopted by EIC
description: EIC obtained minting rights and adopted the Vijayanagara-era Pagoda system (3.4g gold) = 36 silver Fanams; 1 Fanam = 80 copper Kasu. This system remained in use for over 150 years, demonstrating the durability of the pre-colonial monetary framework

name: Introduction of Arcot Rupee
description: Madras Presidency begins minting Arcot Rupees alongside Pagodas to facilitate trade with other presidencies using Mughal Rupee system, creating trade friction between regions with different monetary systems

name: Pagoda Demonetized
description: Presidency stops accepting Pagodas and Fanams, standardizes on Silver Rupees and copper Cash

name: Uniform Coinage Act
description: All presidencies adopt identical standardized coins: 1 Rupee = 16 Annas = 64 Paisa = 192 Pie

name: End of Free Coinage (Fiat Transition)
description: Coins no longer derive value from intrinsic metal content; India transitions from free coinage (where metal value equals face value) to fiat currency backed by government authority

name: Battle of Tallikota. Vijayanagara Falls
description: Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara Empire, leads to fragmentation into Nayak dynasties

name: Nayak Dynasties Emerge
description: Four independent Nayak kingdoms established across Tamil Nadu after Vijayanagara collapse. Chandragiri controlled the coastal Tondai Nadu region, while Gingee, Madurai, and Thanjavur emerged as independent dynastic powers, rather than mere vassals of Vijayanagara

name: Deccan Sultanates Expand South
description: Golconda takes Tondai Nadu, Bijapur takes Nadu Nadu; Madurai and Thanjavur Nayaks pay tribute

name: Maratha Conquest of Gingee
description: Marathas under Shivaji's leadership conquer Gingee from Bijapur, extending Maratha control into Tamil Nadu

name: Thanjavur Maratha Dynasty Established. Replaces Nayaks
description: Marathas establish dynasty in Thanjavur with Ekoji I (Venkoji), displacing the Nayak dynasty. Under Chhatrapati Shivaji's influence, this marks the consolidation of Maratha power in South India

name: Mughals come to Tamil Nadu: Siege of Gingee
description: Aurangzeb's forces besiege Gingee for 8 years; pyrrhic victory that exhausted Mughal forces and prevented further southern expansion, demonstrating the strategic significance of Gingee as a stronghold. Sivaji's son Sambhaji (Chhava movie) was killed in 1689. His half brother Rajaram escaped to Gingee and made Gingee the capital of Marathas

name: Swarup Singh Bundela - Mansabdar of Gingee
description: Swarup Singh Bundela appointed as Mansabdar and Qiladar (feudatory chief) of Gingee Fort by the Mughals, marking a transition in Gingee's governance

name: Evolution of Madras: Fort St. George Founded
description: Chandragiri Nayak grants 2-mile land to British; they establish Fort St. George and Black Town (George Town). Chandragiri was at this time a Nayak state under nominal Mughal suzerainty

name: Evolution of Madras: Expansion to Coovum Banks
description: Through leases and perwanna (official grants) from Mughal and local authorities, British expand into surrounding regions. The perwanna system allowed British to expand control over specific regions (Mylapore, Egmore) through official imperial sanction

name: Ramnad Declares Independence
description: Sethupathi declares independence from Madurai Nayaks, establishing the Marava kingdom as an independent political entity

name: Fall of Madurai to Nawab
description: Chanda Sahib seizes Madurai through betrayal of Queen Regent Meenakshi (fake Quran trick)

name: Maratha Invasion of Tamil Nadu
description: Thanjavur Marathas call reinforcements from Deccan led by Dost Ali Khan; Marathas kill Nawab of Arcot, capture Chanda Sahib; Nizam drives them out

name: Nizam Drives Out Marathas
description: Nizam of Hyderabad intervenes to drive the Marathas out of Tamil Nadu; restores order after Maratha invasion that killed the Nawab of Arcot and captured Chanda Sahib

name: First Carnatic War / Battle of Adyar
place: Fort St. George, Adyar, Fort St. David, Pondicherry
description: French capture Fort St. George; Battle of Adyar - small French force shatters Nawab's army with field artillery, demonstrating the European military revolution and the tactical superiority of disciplined formations and advanced gunnery. "Europeans ceased being traders with muskets." Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle returns Fort St. George to British.
sideB: British East India Company / Nawab of Arcot

name: Second Carnatic War
description: Succession war. Team France (Chanda Sahib + Muzaffar Jung) vs Team Britain (Wallajah + Nasir Jung). This was fundamentally a proxy war between European powers using Indian princes as proxies to extend their influence and territorial control. Battle of Ambur, Siege of Trichy, Clive's Siege of Arcot, beheading of Chanda Sahib, Mysore siege of Trichy. Treaty of Pondicherry. "European powers moved from players to masters."
sideA: French East India Company / Nawab of Arcot (Chanda Sahib) / Mughal Empire (Muzaffar Jung)
sideB: British East India Company / Nawab of Arcot (Wallajah) / Mughal Empire (Nasir Jung)

name: Second carnatic war: Battle of Ambur
description: French-backed forces defeat British-backed Nawab Anwar-ud-din (killed); Muhammad Ali flees to Trichy
sideA: French East India Company / Nawab of Arcot (Chanda Sahib)

name: Second Carnatic War: Siege of Arcot (Clive)
description: Robert Clive with 200-300 soldiers captures and holds Arcot for 50 days against Chanda Sahib's force of 10,000+ troops, forcing him to pull troops from Trichy siege. This tactical maneuver demonstrates Clive's innovative military strategy and marks a turning point in the war

name: Second Carnatic War: Beheading of Chanda Sahib
description: Manakji, general of Thanjavur Marathas, captures and beheads Chanda Sahib; Wallajah becomes undisputed Nawab

name: Second Carnatic War: Mysore Siege of Trichy
description: Wallajah reneges on promise to Mysore (refused to hand over Trichy); young Haider Ali leads the 3-year siege on Mysore's behalf while Yusuf Khan commands the British-allied forces. This siege showcased Haider Ali's military genius and frustration with Indian powers' unwillingness to honor agreements
sideB: British East India Company / Nawab of Arcot

name: Second Carnatic War: Treaty of Pondicherry
description: Ends Second Carnatic War. French get puppet Nizam + Northern Circars. British install Wallajah. Nawab deeply in debt (Arcot debts).

name: Third Carnatic War / Battle of Wandiwash
description: Count de Lally captures Arcot; British win decisively at Wandiwash; British besiege and raze Pondicherry. French returned in 1763 limited to commercial trade only. Permanently removes French as rival.

name: Evolution of Madras: Wave III British Expansion
description: Military force and treaties bring southern villages under British control. Systematic expansion incorporated strategic regions including Mylapore (ancient Christian stronghold), San Thome (Portuguese settlement), Adyar (southern expansion), and Saidapet (western frontier).

name: Yusuf Khan's Rebellion and Execution
description: Yusuf Khan (Marudhunayagam), a skilled military commander who had served the British with distinction, rebels against British-Nawab control attempting to establish independence in Madurai. This rebellion arose from personal grievances and the broader resentment of foreign domination. Nawab and Company besiege Madurai; internal mutiny by Marchand, Srinivasa Rao, Baba Sahib; Yusuf Khan captured and executed. See also Battle of Kaveripakam (1752).
sideB: British East India Company / Nawab of Arcot

name: Anglo-Mysore Wars Raids on Tamil Nadu
description: Haider Ali and Tipu repeatedly raid Tamil Nadu; tax collection falls ~33%; Dindigul under Mysore since 1755

name: Carnatic Treaty of 1787 - Subsidiary Alliance (de facto)
description: While the term was not in vogue, this was an effective subsidiary alliance. Arcot had to pay the British a hefty fee to support British troops. Arcot had to relinquish all foreign policy. This was a political quarantine

name: First Polygar War
description: Veerapandiya Kattabomman refuses taxes; betrayed by Ettayapuram Polygar and Pudukottai Tondaiman Raja. The war fails to mobilize broader polygar support due to internal divisions and British military superiority, demonstrating how isolated resistance could be crushed without unified opposition.

name: Fall of Mysore: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
description: Tipu Sultan killed; British claim to find correspondence between Tipu and Arcot Nawab

name: Second Polygar War
description: Marudhu brothers + escaped Kattabomman associates resist British; Ramnad, Pudukottai, Ettayapuram allied with British; Polygar leaders caught and hanged; Polygar system replaced by Ryotwari (direct cultivation system replacing feudal intermediaries, introducing new administrative and taxation structures)
sideB: British East India Company / Ramnad (Sethupathi) / Pudukottai / Ettayapuram

name: Carnatic Treaty: Annexation of Carnatic Region By British
description: British use Tipu-Nawab correspondence as pretext; bypass rightful Nawab Umdat ul-Umara (also known as Azim ud-Daula), install puppet who signs treaty giving full administrative control to British

name: Vellore Mutiny
description: On July 10, Tipu's sons stationed at Vellore; Sepoys banned from beards/religious marks; massacre of approximately 200 British soldiers; put down by different British garrison with Indian Sepoys. This mutiny is considered a precursor to the later Sepoy Mutiny (1857), sharing similar grievances about religious and cultural restrictions on Indian soldiers.

name: Evolution of Madras: Expansion to Triplicane
description: After the Sultanate of Golconda conquered the region from the Vijayanagara remnants, the British negotiated a lease for Triplicane, establishing control over this important trading center and sacred temple site of Lord Srinivasa.

name: St. Thomas the Apostle Visits Madras Region
description: Apostle Thomas reportedly arrives in India via the spice trade route, establishes Christian communities in Kerala and Madras. Martyred in Mylapore. San Thome Cathedral built over his alleged tomb. One of the earliest documented foreign contacts with South India.

name: Vasco da Gama Arrives in Calicut
description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, establishing the first direct European sea route to India. Opens the era of European maritime trade and eventual colonization of the subcontinent. The pepper he brought back sold for 60x the cost of the entire expedition.

name: Portuguese Establish Goa
description: Albuquerque captures Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, establishing it as the capital of Portuguese India. Becomes the hub of Portuguese trade and missionary activity in Asia for the next 450 years.

name: English East India Company Founded
description: Queen Elizabeth I grants charter to 'The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'. A joint-stock company with limited liability - investors could only lose their investment, not personal assets. This structure enabled massive capital pooling for risky overseas ventures.

name: Dutch East India Company (VOC) Founded
description: VOC established as first true joint-stock company with permanent capital and tradeable shares. At peak, VOC was worth ~$7.9 trillion in today's money. Controlled spice trade across Southeast Asia and maintained significant presence in South India (Pulicat, Pondicherry, Cochin).

name: Bombay Acquired by English
description: Bombay transferred from Portugal to England as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry to King Charles II. Later leased to the East India Company. Becomes a major British trading post alongside Madras and Calcutta.

name: Death of Aurangzeb / Mughal Fragmentation
description: Aurangzeb dies after 49-year reign; Mughal Empire rapidly fragments. Provincial governors (including Nizam of Hyderabad and Nawab of Arcot) become de facto independent. Creates the power vacuum that European companies exploit in South India.

name: Nader Shah Invades and Loots Delhi
description: Persian emperor Nader Shah invades Mughal India, sacks Delhi, and loots the Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond. Removes any remaining illusion of Mughal central authority. Accelerates the independence of provincial governors across India, including in South India.

name: Battle of Plassey
description: Robert Clive defeats Nawab of Bengal Siraj ud-Daulah through conspiracy with Mir Jafar. EIC gains control of Bengal's revenues - the richest province in India. Funds from Bengal finance British military campaigns across India including the Carnatic Wars in South India.
sideA: British East India Company / Mir Jafar

name: Battle of Buxar
description: EIC defeats combined forces of Mughal Emperor, Nawab of Awadh, and Nawab of Bengal. Grants EIC the Diwani (tax collection rights) over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. Transforms the Company from a trading entity into a territorial power with sovereign revenue authority.
sideB: Mughal Emperor / Nawab of Awadh / Nawab of Bengal

name: Battle of Gingee - Death of Raja Desing (Desingaraja)
description: Nawab Sadatullah Khan demands 70 lakh rupees in tribute arrears from young Raja Desing (Tej Singh), son of Swarup Singh. Desing refuses and meets the Nawab in open battle with just 350 horses and 500 troopers against 8,000 horsemen and 10,000 sepoys. Desing is killed at age 22. His wife commits Sati. Despite defeat, he becomes a Tamil folk hero immortalized in ballads (Desingu Raja Kavadi Chindu). Gingee passes to the Nawab of Arcot.

name: EIC establish first factory in South India
description: Machillipatanam was an established trading hub in Golconda. It was a port on the Krishna river where it empties into Bay of Bengal

name: EIC acquire Fort St. David from Marathas
description: In need of hard cash to fight the Mughals, Gingee Marathas auction of Cuddalore and surrounding villages. After a fierce auction between French, English and Dutch, EIC wins out

name: Madurai Nayak Appointed
description: Rivalry between Madurai Pandya and Thanjavur Chandrashekara. Pandya calls Vijayangar Krishnadevaraya for help. He sends his General. After accomplishing mission, he appoints himself King. Krishnadevaraya sends his own son to fight his father. Son, Viswanatha Nayak, wins and becomes first Nayak

name: Thanjavur Nayak splits from Madurai
description: Madurai province that is ruled by Visvanatha Nayak is reorganized to form a new province under Sevappa Nayak.  This happens under the new Vijaynagar Raya, Achyutraya

name: Virginia Company Founded and Jamestown Expedition Starts
description: Auditor Smythe again finds a new company to explore Virginia. First expedition starts from London docks to Chesapeake Bay through the West Indies. On board is John Smith. He meets Pocahontas, who is daughter of the local monarch

name: US Declaration of Independence
description: On July 4 declares independence from Britain. Declaration is written by Thomas Jefferson

name: American War of Independence ends
description: Britain officially recognizes the 13 colonies as United States in the Treaty of Paris

name: Britain parliament and stamp act
description: Parliament passes a stamp act on the 13 colonies. Follows a boycott of good from company and is repealed

name: First Roanoke expedition
description: 107 men sponsored by Sir Thomas Raleigh set out to build a colony in the new world. At this time, Spanish have control all the way up till Florida. So any new colonies have to be higher in latitude or risk getting slaughtered by Spanish.  The first expedition was rescued by Sir Francis Drake and taken back home.

name: Second Roanoke Expedition
description: Ill fated expedition with 110 men. The colony was set up and the ships went back to bring back supplies. Due to Spanish Armada blocking the channel due to Spain war with English, the ships went back only in 1590. Nobody was there!

name: Siege of Yorktown
description:
This was the decisive siege that helped the continental army win war of Independence. The continental army under George Washington with the support of French Army and French Navy laid a siege on the British Forces in Yorktown. Yorktown at that point had almost 1/3rd of all the Birtish forces in North America.  

A very interesting observation is that the person who was leading the British forces was Lord Cornwallis. Lord Cornwallis then goes onto become the Commander-in-Chief of British India and also the Governor General of Bengal Presidency.

name: Lord Cornwallis appointed as Governor General on Bengal Presidency
description: Cornwallis is appointed as the Governor General of Bengal Presidency. More importantly, he is also appointed as the Commander in Chief of all of British India.

name: Battle of Kaveripakam
description:
Reza Sahib, son of Chanda Sahib, fights the British under Clive. Key battle in second carnatic war.

This is likely the battle after which Yusuf Khan (Marudhunayagam) joined the British

name: Punniyappan is sentenced to death
description: Punniyappan is put to death for treachery during the siege of Trichy

name: Abdul Rahim becomes Gov. of Madurai
description: After the death of Nawab Anwaruddin, his son Wallajah becomes the Nawab. His other son Adbul Rahim is appointed Governor of Madurai

name: Alam Khan takes over Madurai
description: Alam Khan, an ally of Chanda Sahib, takes over Madurai from Abdul Rahim
